name: Fox

app.note: The parametric fox of the app puts its standing shoulder joints 0.581 m above the floor (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-mesh/landmark-probe.txt), as the parametric rabbit that set the scale of the rabbit mesh. The reach is the reach of the parametric fox to the middle of the palm in the violin hold (pnpm hold-reach fox-red, hold-reach-parametric.txt). The user has not chosen the arms yet: the reach of the rabbit, 0.377 m, needs a smaller factor.

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm that gives the reach of app.reach from the joints below at the scale of app.shoulders. The first config keeps the arms of the mesh (factor 1), so that pnpm rig-mesh fox --check gives the measured factor for the question to the user. With no --check, pnpm rig-mesh stops when the reach is more than 1% from app.reach.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-mesh/. sections.py gives the cuts at each height: the feet below y 0.05 (the toes forward to z 0.14), the thin shins from 0.05 to 0.11, the wide thighs from 0.13 to the crotch at 0.23, the body from 0.23 to 0.51 (x ±0.093 under the arms), the shoulders at 0.53 to 0.66, the narrow neck at 0.69 to 0.71 (x ±0.089), the head from 0.71 with the muzzle to z 0.28, and the ears apart from 0.91. The trunk joints lie 0.01 to 0.02 behind the middle of the body cut, as in the rabbit, from the hips over the crotch to the chest 0.085 below the shoulder joint. The thigh joint lies at the crotch on the middle of the leg cut, the knee where the thin shin meets the wide thigh, the ankle where the foot starts, and the toes at the ball of the foot. The ear joint lies on the line of the middles of the ear cuts at 0.91 and 0.95, at the top of the head (0.89), and its tail at the ear tip. The cuts at x 0.101 to 0.221 give the middle line of the free arm (sections-x.txt), which leaves the body between x 0.081 and 0.101. The shoulder joint lies on that line, 0.03 inside the root (x 0.07). The wrist lies at the narrow cut where the paw starts (arm-axis.txt, s 0.01 to 0.02), the elbow halfway from the shoulder joint to the wrist and 0.01 behind the line, and the finger joint at the knuckles, 0.03 before the tip of the paw. The tail joint lies at the middle of the root of the tail, between its top on the back (y 0.42, z -0.09) and its bottom on the thighs (y 0.26, z -0.055), and its tail on the middle line of the tail cuts. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. The arm bones take the normal of the palm (palm): the smallest principal direction of the vertices of the left paw, inward and back (facts.txt).

studio.note: The studio has no fox, so the first config takes the seat and the bind arms of the studio rabbit (tools/mesh-rigs/rabbit.json, docs/research/2026-10-13-rabbit-mesh/studio-targets.ts): the world turn of each left leg bone from the bind pose to the first key of the clip reference, and the unit direction of each left arm bone in the bind pose.

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units). The values are the values of the rabbit.

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag behind the line when a joint bends. The value is the value of the rabbit.

weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). The values are the values of the rabbit, scaled by the neck of the fox (x ±0.089 against ±0.077).
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, as in the rabbit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the haunch stays on the seat and only the leg below it turns. The heights take the places of the rabbit ramp along the thigh, from 0.14 of the thigh below the knee to 0.57 of the thigh above it.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones: the cuts of sections.py x show the arm apart from the body from x 0.101 out. Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only: the neck is narrowest at y 0.69 to 0.71, and the cheek fur starts at 0.73. Each ear vertex goes to its ear bone with a ramp over the heights of earBase. The tail ball is the one tail bone of the studio format: the vertices within radius of center and behind the plane z = behind follow the tail only. The ball holds the tail from its tip (y 0.01) to its root on the back (y 0.42), and the plane keeps the backs of the thighs (z -0.04 at y 0.21) out of it.

refine.ringsNote: The first config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh fox --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

flip.note: The long edge of a face of the arms with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind mesh flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane (normals, degrees) and the surface moves at most move (units). The values are the values of the rabbit.

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind mesh with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of a joint of the arms or the legs. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings). The values are the values of the rabbit.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at the samples of a grid of the given steps on the face. A face is dark when its share of samples with a linear luminance below dark is at least eyeShare, and then it takes the mean of its dark samples. Each other face takes the mean of its samples that are not dark. A dark face in the eye box (the left eye at x 0.043, y 0.805 in the front view, mirrored for the right eye) is a face of an eye. A face in the nose box whose color is nearer to the nose color than to white is a face of the nose: the nose of the fox is black, at the tip of the muzzle (y 0.765, z 0.28). Then each face takes the nearest color of a palette of palette colors, from k-means in Oklab.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most this number of points of their edge, lifted this far (units) along the normal of the eye. The values are the values of the rabbit.

chair.note: The chair has the depth of the chair of the rabbit rig (0.13 units), and it is wider, because the haunch of the fox is x ±0.17. Its front edge lies behind the heels of the seated bind. The seat top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat.
